unit: days (half-life of stress deviation from baseline)
basis: Daily-diary work shows stressor-driven negative affect largely resolves within about 1 to 2 days, with a minority of lingering response (Bolger 1989: habituation by day 2 for most events except interpersonal conflict; Leger 2018: next-day carryover is common but partial). Lag-1 daily autocorrelations of negative affect of about 0.3 to 0.6 (assumed, not sourced here) imply half-life = ln2 / -ln(phi) = 0.6 to 1.4 days for mood; stress appraisal tied to ongoing demands and rumination lasts longer (Verduyn 2015: importance and rumination stretch episodes from hours to days). Chronic stress is carried by stressBaseline and the resting-stress terms, so the decay of deviation from baseline can be shorter than 7 days: 3 days is a defensible middle with mood at 1. Note: some figures here come from sources not fetched this session (marked retrieved:false); treat as estimate.

unit: model structure
basis: Affect literature supports exponential-like return to baseline for most emotions with median episode durations of hours and long tails for sadness (about 120 hours) and ruminated events (Verduyn 2015); daily-diary studies show partial next-day carryover (Leger 2018). Adult trajectories can be checked against PSS-10 norms (mean about 12.8 of 40, SD 6.42; Klein 2016). The affine structure is adequate; the gap is a slow component (rumination, chronic burden) which is currently only carried by baselines. recommendedValue: keep group size 20; recognition about 0.9 within 15 years of leaving school, about 0.7 near 50 years
unit: probability a cohort peer is still recognized by name
basis: Class-sized groups average 17 to 22 (NCES), which supports peer group size of 20 for acquaintance. Recognition memory for classmates is high for a long time: about 90% name recognition up to about 15 years after graduation and roughly 60 to 80% after about 47 years (Bahrick 1975, secondary summaries disagree). So generated acquaintance can persist with recognition probability falling from 0.9 to about 0.7 across adulthood. Close friendship needs far more time (Hall 2018: about 50 hours casual, 200+ close), so most generated peers should be acquaintances, not friends.
